all**. Your completion report is the whole deliverable, and three nodes read it as their
input. Report these six sections, under these headings, in this order.

## Why
The manager accumulated these notes across many sessions while supervising real work, and
they have never been read as a set. The user asked for this in their own words: *"go
through them one by one and verify the root cause, group everything by the root cause,
present root cause evidence and suggested fix; make sure the follow-up is not already
mentioned in issues 27 or 28 and check those for overlap as well as additional evidence
for the same or related issues."* The user wants to decide what to fix, and a finding that
cannot be grounded in current code is worth less than nothing to that decision, because it
costs a reader time and erodes trust in the rest.

Every later node in this run cites this report. Fetching once, here, is what stops three
concurrent slices racing the same five checkouts and citing three different commits — and
what lets the finished document say "as of" one commit per repository instead of "as of
whenever each claim happened to be checked".

## Acceptance criteria
- This dispatch creates, modifies and deletes no file anywhere: the report is the whole deliverable, and the only filesystem change it makes is the `.git/` of the five checkouts it fetched.
- The report carries all six named sections in order, each in the line shape this task fixes, so a downstream node can read a field by position.
- The report opens with one ISO-8601 UTC stamp taken before any other work.
- The census names every corpus file with its line count and its owning slice, states the actual number of `followup-*.md` notes, and names any difference between that number and the 23 the brief claims.
- Each of the five repositories is reported with the commit its `origin/main` points at, that commit's date, the newest release tag reachable from it, and how far the checkout's own `HEAD` is from it.
- Each repository's reported commit was produced by a fetch this dispatch performed, and the report says when that fetch happened.
- For every engine the harness pins, the report gives both the pinned version and the version a dispatch on this host actually runs, with the measurement that established the second one quoted.
- The issue index lists every item of #27 and of #28 under the citation vocabulary this task fixes, with each item's claim in one line and the evidence it already carries, and gives both issues' last-updated stamps.
- The basis is established end to end from this host rather than from prose: every commit in it comes from this dispatch's own fetch and every in-force version from the installed binary this host runs.
- No engine checkout changes branch or working tree, and no GitHub issue is created, edited or commented on.
- The dispatch closes with this report as its final completion report, naming what was measured, the evidence for it, that it wrote no file, and anything it could not establish and why.

## Additional info

### Operational notes for this host

**Iterate on the judged tier alone. Never loop on the complete gate.** This is the single
most expensive mistake made in this workstream: one node ran the complete gate three times
to learn its lint findings — ~28 minutes a round, each round ending on the judged tier
after the deterministic tier had already passed — and then cleared its last two findings in
four minutes once it split them. Your loop is

    just lint-llm-diff "$BASE"

alone, about two minutes a roll. The complete gate is `complete_gate` below, and you run it
exactly **once**, at the end, to confirm.

**Define the complete gate once, before you start, and never spell it out again.** Both of
its parts vary by repository — the base branch is not always `main`, and `just gate` already
runs the judged tier in some repositories while in others that tier is a separate step — so
both live in one definition and everything below calls it:

    BASE=origin/master   # confirm it: git remote show origin | sed -n 's/.*HEAD branch: /origin\//p'
    complete_gate() { just bootstrap && just gate && just lint-llm-diff "$BASE"; }

It has to run as **one invocation**. A worker that runs the parts separately is failed for
never having run the gate end to end, however green each part was on its own — which is why
nothing below ever names a part of the chain instead of the whole of it.

**Never run two gates at once.** This repository's e2e configs bind fixed ports
(4301, 4310, 4314, 4316, 4321, ...). A second concurrent gate does not queue — it fails
with `http://127.0.0.1:43xx/... is already used`, and both runs lose. Two publications
raced this way on 2026-08-18 and each burned 13 minutes to reach that error.

**Wait on a gate with a sentinel file, never a `pgrep` pattern that matches your own
poll.** `pgrep -f "just gate"` matches the shell running the loop, so the loop never
exits. That has wedged four workers here. Background `complete_gate` itself — the whole
chain, so what you waited on is the same command the paragraphs above call complete:

    ( complete_gate > /tmp/gate.log 2>&1; echo $? > /tmp/gate.exit ) &
    until [ -f /tmp/gate.exit ]; do sleep 20; done

**Root-owned files after a container run.** The pre-push visual guard captures in Docker
as root and can leave `.nx/` and `dist/` unwritable, failing the *next* gate with `NX
Permission denied (os error 13)`. There is no passwordless sudo; repair from inside a
container:

    docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble \
      chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w

**If a test fails in a way that makes no sense, check the host before the test.** On
2026-08-19 two publication attempts against the same already-green branch failed on two
unrelated tests — a 5-second timeout, then a browser remote that never came up — and both
were written up as flakes. The host was at 197G/197G, and the next attempt said so
outright with `No space left on device`. A full disk does not announce itself to a test
runner; it announces itself as an unrelated test failing. One command rules it out:

    df -h /home .

**The judged tier is nondeterministic.** It has already returned opposite verdicts on an
identical diff in this workstream. Clear the findings it names, then stop — do not re-run
hunting a clean sheet, and never suppress a rule to move a number. If a rule looks wrong
or misapplied, say so with evidence rather than editing it.

**Publication goes through the harness.** No `git push`, no `gh pr create`, no `gh pr
merge`. Finish the branch, commit everything, leave the tree clean, and report — the
lifecycle publishes it after you settle. Publication is explicitly **not** yours to
perform and **not** part of your acceptance criteria.

### State the bar in `## Acceptance criteria`, not only here

A judge reads this node's `## Acceptance criteria` and its own review bar. Where the
criteria are silent about something the bar demands, it imports the demand and applies its
own reading of it — and finished, gate-green work has been failed twice that way: once for
running the gate's parts separately, and once for never having *"provided a final verified
completion report"*, a demand in neither the task nor the shared completion clause.

So every demand this node will be held to is stated as a criterion of its own, including
the two the bar makes of every implementation dispatch:

- the behavior this node adds is **proven end to end** by a test or journey that drives the
  real interface, rather than by inspection;
- the dispatch closes with a **final completion report** naming what was verified and the
  evidence for it.

Criteria state properties of the finished tree; the commands that produce them belong in
this section. `just check-plan <plan.json>` refuses a task whose criteria omit a demand its
resolved review bar — or this appendix — makes of it.

### For this node

**Write exactly one path, or none.** `scratch/triage-by-root-cause.md` is the only file this run may create
or modify anywhere on this host. No worksheets, no notes, no scratch directory, no backup,
no temporary file, no redirected log — not under `scratch/`, not under `/tmp`, not
anywhere. If your `## What` does not name that path, you write **nothing at all** and your
report is your whole deliverable. Read with tools that read; do not stage intermediate
results on disk. The two writes this run does not own are the engine's own journal under
`runs/` and the `.git/` of a checkout that gets fetched — neither is yours to make.

**This is a read-only research dispatch.** It changes no file tracked by any repository, so
the complete-gate and publication paragraphs above do not apply to it: there is no finished
tree for a gate to run over and nothing to publish. Do not run a repository gate, do not
commit, and do not push.

**The corpus exists in exactly one place.** `/home/nick/projects/ai-orchestrator/scratch/`

**Never** modify, create, or delete a tracked file in this repository or in the four engine

**Your review bar and this task agree, and here is the reconciliation.** The bar asks that

deliverable, not a project-file change: it is gitignored working scratch, and the corpus
beside it is the same. Say so in your completion report, and name the file you wrote — or
say that you wrote none — so the reconciliation is on the record rather than left to be
inferred.

**Your completion report is an interface, not a summary.** A downstream node reads it as
its whole input. Emit every line the shape below asks for, in that shape, in full. Do not
abbreviate it, do not replace a list with a count, and do not say a section is available on
request. Length is expected and correct.

**Ask rather than guess.** If a fork in this task could change what the user decides, put
one blocking question to the manager with `"$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER"` instead of picking a
branch silently.

### Reading an upstream node's report

Nothing in this run passes work through a file. A finished node's whole output is its
**final completion report**, which the engine keeps for the life of the run. Read one like
this — it creates nothing, and it is the same reading measured against a live run before
this plan was written:

    ROOT="/home/nick/projects/ai-orchestrator/runs/$ONEPIPELINE_RUN_ID"
    python3 - "$ROOT" <NODE-ID> <<'PY'
    import glob, json, os, sys
    root, node = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    graphs = []

        for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "reports", graph + "-*.json"))):
            said = [m["content"] for m in json.load(open(path))["transcript"]["messages"]
                    if m.get("role") == "assistant"]
            if said:

    PY

`ONEPIPELINE_RUN_ID` is exported to every node dispatch on the adopted onepipeline.

**If a report you depend on is missing, unreadable, or looks summarized rather than
complete** — the finding count it states does not match the number of finding lines it
carries — do not proceed on what you can salvage. Put one blocking question to the manager
with `"$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER"` naming the node and what is missing. A silently short

## Citations, and the bar this node is actually judged against

Your review bar demands **specific source citations** and that **confirmed facts are
distinguished from inferences**. A previous dispatch of this node was failed for producing
a census without them, so treat the following as acceptance criteria of equal weight:

- Every factual claim about a repository's contents cites it as
  `repo@<short-sha>:<path>:<line>` and quotes the line it relies on. A commit id alone is

- Every claim about a pinned or in-force version quotes the exact bytes that establish it

  An inference presented as a fact is the failure this bar exists to prevent.

## Report every command honestly, including the ones that did not succeed

The same dispatch was also failed for claiming every fetch exited 0 while separately

# CITATION CONVENTION

```
<repo>@<sha>:<path>:<line>
```

A citation quotes the line it relies on. A commit id alone is not a citation; a path with no line is not a citation; a line number with no quoted text is not a citation, because a reader cannot check it without opening the file.

Use the short shas fixed by REPO SNAPSHOT above and no others: `ai-orchestrator@e2327da`, `onepipeline@e435f52`, `onevcs@def750e`, `oneagentgraph@6b62df7`, `oneharness@75c16a4`. Read source with `git show <sha>:<path>` rather than from a checkout's working tree or its local `main` — three of the four engine checkouts are behind their origin (onepipeline 8, onevcs 18, oneagentgraph 4 commits).

    12	
    13	**The principle we want:** every point at which a publication can fail must be *observed*, must *capture its evidence*, and must *route that evidence to a live worker*. Today we do the first inconsistently, the second almost nowhere, and the third only by accident.

    15	## Audit of every failure surface
    16	
    17	One surface already does this correctly — `crates/onevcs/src/integrate.rs:424` stores the gate's real output as an artifact, puts a `preserved_log` path on the event, and attaches the artifact. That is the model. Nothing else copies it.

    21	| gate command | yes | **yes** — `store_artifact("log", &verdict.output)` + `preserved_log` | yes |

    28	
    29	The re-dispatch machinery is already built and correct. `gate-failed` and `checks-failed` are *preserving* outcomes: the branch is kept, mode is `continue`, and **no steps are recorded as completed**, so the continuation re-dispatches them — `docs/repo-lifecycle.md:1219`, *"skipping them as completed would republish the identical rejected tree."*

# CITATION CONVENTION

```
<repo>@<sha>:<path>:<line>
```

A citation quotes the line it relies on. A commit id alone is not a citation; a path with no line is not a citation; a line number with no quoted text is not a citation, because a reader cannot check it without opening the file.

Use the short shas fixed by REPO SNAPSHOT above and no others: `ai-orchestrator@e2327da`, `onepipeline@e435f52`, `onevcs@def750e`, `oneagentgraph@6b62df7`, `oneharness@75c16a4`. Read source with `git show <sha>:<path>` rather than from a checkout's working tree or its local `main` — three of the four engine checkouts are behind their origin (onepipeline 8, onevcs 18, oneagentgraph 4 commits).

Three shapes that are deliberately **not** `<repo>@<sha>:<path>:<line>`, because they cannot be:

- **Corpus notes.** `scratch/` is gitignored and in no commit. Cite as `scratch/<file>:<line>` and say the file is untracked working scratch.
